ranking_vs_relevance.note: similarity() compares anatomic_location on the pancreas only; relevant() reads it on every shared organ, so a sub-site change on a kidney or a liver moves the gold standard without moving any score

steps.what_changed: the manuscript's own pool, corpora and scorer, recomputed
114 FLARE23 twins of the query set removed; records, scorer and sub-site words unchanged
a void sub-site axis dropped from the organ mean

circularity.note: relevant() derives the gold standard from the same four fields similarity() ranks on, so the benchmark tests whether the ranker behaves as designed and cannot test whether the phenotypes are correct

held_out_axis_relevance.definition: relevance = agreement on ONE axis on a shared organ (the delivered rule needs >=2 agreements over all four); the ranker still scores all four axes, so this weakens rather than removes the dependence - the only fully disjoint variant would also have to withhold the axis from the score, which changes the system under test

external_relevance_unavailable.why: scan identity is the one relevance signal in hand that is independent of the ranked fields, and the pool has none left: de-duplication removed exactly the FLARE23 twins of the query set, so no twin pair has both members in the 1,311 pool

cannot_produce: a clinician-adjudicated relevance set: none exists for these 1,311 cases
a scan-identity (twin) relevance set: 0 of the 521 census pairs have both members in the de-duplicated pool

a relevance definition fully disjoint from the score: every field the records carry that relevance could be built from is a field the score already reads; withholding one from the score changes the system under test rather than the evaluation of it
